title: Step Supporting Validator Unit Behavioral Contract

scope.purpose: Define the behavioral responsibilities, invocation boundary, validation result semantics, and provenance obligations of an optional Step Supporting Validator Unit.
scope.appliesTo: A concrete Step specialization that selects and uses one or more Step Supporting Validator Unit instances.

validatorUnitInstance.meaning: One concrete runtime instance that performs a specialized validation responsibility.

validatorInvocation.meaning: One distinct attempt to invoke a validator-unit instance for one authorized validation request under one specific association.

associationContext.meaning: The identity-bearing association under which the invocation is authorized, including the Step-owned target scope to which that association applies.

targetContext.meaning: The concrete validation-relevant context or target information supplied for the associated target scope. It is distinct from the target's identity.

validationOutcome.meaning: The domain-specific conclusion produced by applying the validator's validation semantics to the supplied validation input and context.
validationOutcome.constraint: The common contract does not define a universal pass/fail boolean, severity model, or interpretation.

validationEvidence.meaning: Optional information supporting, explaining, or substantiating the validation outcome, as defined by the concrete validator specialization.

validationResult.meaning: The structured result of one normally completed validator invocation, including its outcome and the provenance needed to attribute that outcome to the invocation and its authorized association.

optionality: A Step is not required to select, provision, associate, or invoke any Validator Unit.
The existence of this contract does not make validation mandatory for every Step.
A concrete Step selects Validator Units only when its processing responsibility requires their validation capabilities.
behavioralSpecialization: This contract defines reusable behavioral obligations and boundaries, not a universal validation algorithm or domain model.
The concrete Validator Unit specialization defines what is validated, the meaning of its outcome, the structure of its evidence, and the validation rules applied.
The concrete Step defines how the selected Validator Unit is used within its own processing composition.
compositionAuthority: Step Composition determines when an invocation is authorized, selects the applicable association, supplies the invocation context, and coordinates consumption and retention of the returned result.
The Validator Unit owns the execution of its specialized validation semantics and the production of its Validator Unit Validation Result.
The Validator Unit does not own Step flow control, Step orchestration, association management, or Step-level result aggregation.
identitySeparation: validatorUnitIdentity, validatorUnitAssociationIdentity, associationTargetIdentity, stepInstanceIdentity, and validatorInvocationIdentity identify different architectural facts and must not be conflated.
A validator invocation is bound to exactly one association context, even when the same validator instance participates in multiple associations.
Repeated invocations under the same association receive distinct validatorInvocationIdentity values.
resultIndependence: A Validator Unit Validation Result is distinct from SPUExecutionResult, StepCompositionFlowResult, StepValidatorResult, StepExecutionResult, ErrorResult, and ErrorHandlerResult.
A validation outcome is not itself a Step flow-control decision.
A validation result may be retained as historical evidence after its association has ended and after its validator instance has been released.

behavioralContract.capability: A Validator Unit evaluates a supplied validation input in the context of one authorized Step-owned target association and produces a specialized validation outcome with the provenance required to interpret that outcome.
responsibilities: Apply the validation rules and semantics defined by the concrete Validator Unit specialization.
Use only the validation input and target context supplied or made accessible through the authorized invocation boundary.
Treat the supplied association context as the scope under which the invocation is authorized; do not select or substitute another association or target.
Produce a structured validation result for each invocation that completes normally, including the required invocation and association provenance.
Preserve the semantic distinction between the validation outcome and any evidence explaining that outcome.
Expose or return the result through the interaction mechanism defined by the concrete specialization without assuming ownership of Step-level aggregation.
Report invocation inability or implementation-level failure through the applicable failure/exception boundary without fabricating a validation outcome.
nonResponsibilities: Selecting, creating, changing, rebinding, or ending Validator Unit Associations.
Provisioning, admitting, retaining, quiescing, or releasing the Validator Unit instance.
Choosing invocation timing, frequency, ordering, or coordination with SPU execution.
Choosing Step transitions or deciding whether a validation outcome terminates, pauses, retries, or otherwise changes Step flow.
Aggregating results from multiple Validator Unit instances into StepValidatorResult.
Constructing StepExecutionResult or modifying its other aggregate fields.
Creating SPU errors or Step errors merely because a validation outcome represents an invalid or unacceptable condition.
Defining a universal validation algorithm, pass/fail convention, severity taxonomy, or evidence format.

invocationContract.invocationAuthority: Step Composition exclusively authorizes and coordinates invocation of a Validator Unit within the owning Step.

conceptualInvocationBoundary.name: ValidatorUnitInvocation
conceptualInvocationBoundary.description: A logical invocation boundary consisting of a distinct invocation identity, one authorized association context, validation input, and any specialization-defined invocation context.
implementationFreedom: The contract does not require a separately allocated request object, a particular method name, or a universal callable signature.
The concrete specialization may use a direct method call, an interface, a message, or another explicit interaction mechanism appropriate to its implementation.
The interaction mechanism must preserve the semantic input and identity obligations defined by this contract.

requiredInvocationInformation.name: stepInstanceIdentity
requiredInvocationInformation.meaning: Identifies the owning Step instance within which the invocation is authorized.
requiredInvocationInformation.requirement: Must be available to the invocation and result provenance where required to distinguish Step instances.

requiredInvocationInformation.name: validatorUnitIdentity
requiredInvocationInformation.meaning: Identifies the concrete Validator Unit instance being invoked.
requiredInvocationInformation.requirement: Must identify the actual runtime instance performing the validation.

requiredInvocationInformation.name: validatorUnitAssociationIdentity
requiredInvocationInformation.meaning: Identifies the particular association that authorizes this invocation.
requiredInvocationInformation.requirement: Exactly one association identity must be bound to each invocation.

requiredInvocationInformation.name: associationTargetIdentity
requiredInvocationInformation.meaning: Identifies the Step-owned target scope bound to the selected association.
requiredInvocationInformation.sourceAuthority: The authoritative association record maintained by Step Composition.
requiredInvocationInformation.requirement: Must correspond to the target bound to validatorUnitAssociationIdentity; it must not be independently substituted by the Validator Unit.

requiredInvocationInformation.name: validatorInvocationIdentity
requiredInvocationInformation.sourceAuthority: Step Composition or the Step-defined invocation identity mechanism.
requiredInvocationInformation.requirement: Must be assigned or reserved before invocation begins and remain stable throughout invocation and result attribution.

requiredInvocationInformation.name: validationInput
requiredInvocationInformation.meaning: The data, values, artifact, or references that the Validator Unit must evaluate.
requiredInvocationInformation.sourceAuthority: Defined and supplied by the concrete Step's invocation design.
requiredInvocationInformation.requirement: Its type, ownership, mutability, and validity rules are specialization-specific.

requiredInvocationInformation.name: targetContext
requiredInvocationInformation.meaning: The validation-relevant context for the associated target scope, beyond the target's identity alone.
requiredInvocationInformation.sourceAuthority: Defined and supplied or exposed by the concrete Step's invocation design.
requiredInvocationInformation.requirement: Its representation, completeness, freshness, mutability, and access mode are specialization-specific.

specializationDefinedInvocationInformati: Additional validation parameters, policies, configuration, or environmental context required by the concrete Validator Unit.
A target snapshot, immutable view, borrowed reference, handle, query interface, or other target-context access mechanism where required.
Correlation information connecting the validation request to a particular Step or SPU processing activity, if the concrete Step requires it.
Invocation constraints such as deadline, cancellation capability, or resource budget only where explicitly defined by the concrete specialization.
associationAndTargetBindingRules: Step Composition selects an association that is valid for the Validator Unit instance and target scope at the point invocation is authorized.
The invocation is correlated with that exact validatorUnitAssociationIdentity and associationTargetIdentity pair.
The Validator Unit must not infer the target identity from validationInput when an authoritative associationTargetIdentity is supplied.
The targetContext must represent or provide access to the target scope identified by associationTargetIdentity; the concrete Step defines how that correspondence is established and maintained.
If the same Validator Unit instance has multiple active associations, the invocation context must disambiguate the selected association explicitly.
An invocation already authorized under one association must not be silently redirected to another association if associations change while work is in progress.
The concrete Step defines whether the invocation receives a target snapshot or accesses a live target context, including any consistency guarantees.
authorizationAndReadiness: The Validator Unit may be invoked only when its instance is admitted and satisfies the applicable readiness conditions under the Lifecycle Contract.
The selected association must be valid and usable for new invocation under the Association Contract.
Step Composition is responsible for ensuring these preconditions before authorizing invocation.

The Validator Unit may reject or fail an invocation that violates its declared implementation-specific readiness, concurrency, or input constraints; such rejection is not a validation outcome unless the concrete specialization explicitly defines it as one.

invocationCardinality.commonRule: One invocation identity identifies one invocation attempt. A normally completed invocation produces one structured Validator Unit Validation Result, whose outcome may itself represent zero, one, or multiple validation findings according to the specialization.
notMandated: Whether a validation request is retried as a new invocation.
Whether a Validator Unit instance may serve multiple associations concurrently.
invocationCardinality.specializationObligation: The concrete Step and Validator Unit specialization define invocation scheduling, concurrency, reentrancy, retry identity, and any asynchronous completion/correlation mechanism.

validationResultContract.meaning: A structured, invocation-scoped result describing the validation outcome produced by one normally completed Validator Unit invocation.

requiredElements.name: stepInstanceIdentity
requiredElements.meaning: The owning Step instance under which the validation was performed.

requiredElements.name: validatorUnitIdentity
requiredElements.meaning: The Validator Unit instance that performed the validation.

requiredElements.name: validatorUnitAssociationIdentity
requiredElements.meaning: The exact association under which the invocation was authorized.

requiredElements.name: associationTargetIdentity
requiredElements.meaning: The target scope to which the association applied.

requiredElements.name: validatorInvocationIdentity
requiredElements.meaning: The distinct invocation attempt that produced this result.

requiredElements.name: validationOutcome
requiredElements.meaning: The specialization-defined validation conclusion. Its type and interpretation are not standardized by this common contract.

optionalElements.name: validationEvidence
optionalElements.meaning: Specialization-defined evidence, findings, diagnostics, measurements, or explanations supporting the validation outcome.

optionalElements.name: validationSubjectReference
optionalElements.meaning: A reference or identity for the particular subject evaluated, when it is distinct from the association target or necessary for interpretation.

optionalElements.name: completionMetadata
optionalElements.meaning: Specialization-defined information needed to interpret when or under which validation conditions the result was produced.

resultSemantics: The result represents validation semantics, not invocation infrastructure status.

A validation outcome that expresses rejection, invalidity, non-compliance, or another negative domain conclusion is still a normally produced validation result, not automatically an invocation failure.
The common contract does not require validationOutcome to be boolean, nor does it prescribe names such as Passed, Failed, Valid, or Invalid.
An invocation that does not complete normally does not fabricate a Validator Unit Validation Result.

If a specialization supports partial findings or multiple result fragments before invocation completion, it must define their explicit result/custody contract; the common contract does not imply implicit partial-result publication.
identityAndProvenanceInvariants: Every result must identify exactly one validator invocation.
The validatorUnitIdentity in the result must identify the instance that actually performed the invocation.
The validatorUnitAssociationIdentity and associationTargetIdentity must match the association context bound to that invocation.
The result's provenance must not be rewritten if the association later changes or ends.
Two results from two different invocations must remain distinguishable even if they have identical validation outcomes and were produced under the same association.
Historical references to the identities do not imply that the instance remains alive or that the association remains active.

productionOwnership: The Validator Unit owns the validation computation and the construction of its specialized Validator Unit Validation Result.
While the result is being constructed and before it is handed off through the defined invocation boundary, the Validator Unit is responsible for preserving the integrity of the result.
The Validator Unit must not expose a result as complete before all fields required by its specialized result contract and provenance obligations are established.
handoffToStepComposition: For a normally completed invocation, the Validator Unit returns or otherwise publishes the complete result through the interaction mechanism defined by the concrete specialization.
Upon successful handoff/acceptance, Step Composition becomes responsible for custody, retention, and subsequent use of that result within the Step.

The concrete specialization defines the precise handoff/acceptance point and whether the mechanism transfers ownership, transfers an immutable value, or establishes another explicit custody arrangement.
A result must not be treated as transferred merely because a handoff was attempted when the selected interaction mechanism can report rejection or indeterminate acceptance.

If the interaction mechanism permits an indeterminate handoff outcome, the concrete Step must define reconciliation and recovery ownership so that a produced result is neither silently lost nor aggregated twice.
postHandoffResponsibilities: Step Composition retains the result according to the concrete Step's result/evidence retention policy.
Step Composition determines whether and how the result contributes to StepValidatorResult and ultimately to the optional validatorResult element of StepExecutionResult.
Step Composition may correlate the result with other SPU or supporting-unit results without changing the original validation outcome or provenance.
The Validator Unit does not retain ownership of a handed-off result solely because its own runtime instance remains alive.
The Validator Unit does not construct or mutate StepValidatorResult or StepExecutionResult.
preservationRules: A result successfully handed off to Step Composition remains subject to the Step's retention contract even if a later internal operation fails or throws an exception.
A later invocation failure does not authorize discarding a previously accepted validation result.
Releasing the Validator Unit instance does not delete, mutate, or invalidate a result whose retention is still required.
If result content depends on instance-owned resources, the concrete specialization must define how the content is detached or materialized before those resources are released.
An exception after a result has been accepted must not revoke or rewrite that accepted result.

failureAndExceptionBoundary.principle: Validation conclusions, invocation failures, and lifecycle failures are distinct categories.
rules: A validation outcome expressing an unacceptable condition is not, by itself, an exception or execution failure.

Input rejection, inability to access target context, internal validator failure, cancellation, and other abnormal invocation conditions are classified by the concrete Validator Unit and Step specialization.
The common contract does not prescribe a universal exception taxonomy, error object, retry policy, or conversion of exceptions into Error Occurrences.
An exception or abnormal termination does not automatically produce a validation result.
A thrown exception remains distinct from any validation result already handed off and accepted before the exception occurred.

If the concrete interaction mechanism allows partial result production before abnormal termination, its specialization must define the custody and recovery obligations for those partial results explicitly.
The Validator Unit does not decide whether Step Composition continues, retries, branches, or terminates the Step after an invocation failure.

validatorUnitResponsibilities: Use only the association context selected and supplied by Step Composition for the invocation.
Preserve the association and target identities in the result provenance.
Report an unusable or inconsistent association context to Step Composition without independently changing association state.
associationContract.explicitBoundary: The Association Contract governs applicability, target binding, association identity, validity, and dissociation. This Behavioral Contract governs what the Validator Unit does during an invocation under an already-authorized association.

validatorUnitResponsibilities: Satisfy its declared readiness and invocation-safety requirements.
Preserve result integrity through the defined handoff boundary.
Report inability to accept or continue work under its specialized behavior.
lifecycleContract.explicitBoundary: The Lifecycle Contract governs provisioning, preparation, readiness, admission, availability, reuse, quiescence, and release. This Behavioral Contract does not establish or alter instance lifecycle state.

stepCompositionAuthority: Step Composition authorizes invocation and selects the applicable association.
Step Composition supplies or makes available validationInput and targetContext under the concrete Step's interaction design.
Step Composition retains accepted results and decides their Step-specific use and aggregation.
Step Composition coordinates invocation failures with the concrete Step's flow and recovery policy.
Step Composition coordinates association and lifecycle changes without delegating their authority to the Validator Unit.

retentionAndHistoricalInterpretation.principle: A validation result and its provenance may outlive both the association under which it was produced and the Validator Unit runtime instance that produced it.
rules: The concrete Step defines the retention duration, storage representation, access policy, and release conditions for validation results and evidence.
Any retained result must preserve the required provenance identities for as long as the result may be observed or referenced.
An ended association remains identifiable as historical provenance but cannot authorize new invocations.
A released Validator Unit instance may remain referenced by historical result identity without remaining callable.

Retained result content must remain interpretable without requiring the original Validator Unit runtime instance to remain alive, unless the concrete Step independently defines another explicit dependency.
The concrete Step defines whether results are immutable after handoff; the common contract requires that historical provenance and outcome semantics not be silently rewritten.
retentionAndHistoricalInterpretation.retentionAuthority: Step Composition applies the concrete Step's result/evidence retention policy. This contract defines attribution and integrity obligations but does not prescribe a storage mechanism or universal retention period.

required: Define the validation responsibility, subject, and rules implemented by the concrete Validator Unit.
Define the concrete validationInput type, ownership, mutability, and validity requirements.
Define the targetContext representation and how it is bound to associationTargetIdentity.
Define the concrete invocation interaction mechanism while preserving all required invocation identities and context.
Define the validationOutcome type and its domain-specific interpretation without relying on an assumed common boolean convention.
Define the validationEvidence structure, if evidence is produced, and whether it is optional or required.
Define any additional result fields and any validation subject identity distinct from the association target.
Define invocation completion and the exact result handoff/acceptance point.
Define result custody and recovery behavior if handoff acceptance can be rejected or remain indeterminate.
Define invocation failure, exception, cancellation, and partial-result behavior where applicable.
Define synchronous/asynchronous behavior, concurrency, reentrancy, and retry identity rules where applicable.
Define how Step Composition consumes and aggregates accepted Validator Unit Validation Results into the Step-specific StepValidatorResult.
Define result/evidence retention and detachment requirements consistently with the instance Lifecycle Contract.
specializationRequirements.completionRule: A concrete Validator Unit specialization is behaviorally complete when its invocation inputs, association/target binding, outcome/evidence semantics, result provenance, custody boundary, and applicable failure/concurrency behavior are explicit and consistent with the Association and Lifecycle Contracts.

explicitNonGoals: No mandatory Validator Unit for every Step.
No universal method signature, request class, response class implementation, or transport protocol.
No universal validation algorithm, boolean pass/fail result, severity taxonomy, or evidence schema.
No universal target snapshot, live-reference, handle, or target-context access mechanism.
No universal invocation order, frequency, trigger, scheduler, or execution topology.
No universal synchronous, asynchronous, concurrent, or reentrant execution requirement.
No association creation, mutation, rebinding, or dissociation authority for the Validator Unit.
No instance provisioning, admission, reuse, quiescence, or release authority for the Validator Unit.
No Step flow-control, branching, retry, termination, or recovery authority for the Validator Unit.
No construction of StepValidatorResult or StepExecutionResult by the Validator Unit.
No automatic conversion of validation outcomes, invocation failures, or exceptions into SPUError or StepError occurrences.
No mandatory global result registry, validation manager, central mediator, or universal result-storage mechanism.

references.relationship: Association identity, target binding, applicability, validity, and dissociation boundaries.
Instance readiness, admission, invocation eligibility, quiescence, reuse, release, and evidence lifetime separation.
Step Composition authority over internal invocation coordination, result collection, flow, and lifecycle decisions.
Owning Step boundary and Stage-facing interface.
SPU boundary when an SPU instance is the validator association target.
Step-level validatorResult aggregation boundary and distinction between Validator Unit results and StepValidatorResult.

openDesignDetails: Define the concrete Validator Unit invocation input and target-context types for each Step specialization.
Define the concrete Validator Unit Validation Result type and the Step-specific StepValidatorResult aggregation model.
Define result handoff mechanics for any specialization whose interaction model is asynchronous or can report indeterminate acceptance.
Define the concrete Step's retention and release policy for validation result content and evidence.
